newsitem.title: CANADA: CBRS sets rating for CP Rail certificates.
newsitem.headline: CBRS sets rating for CP Rail certificates.

text.p: Canadian Bond Rating Service said on Tuesday it assigned an A rating to Canadian Pacific Ltd unit CP Rail's US$123.1 million pass-through certificates series 1997-A1 and 1997-A2.

The certificates, being offered only in the United States, are to be used to refinance the railway company's debt arranged in conjuction with the capital lease of 83 General Electric Co diesel locomotives in 1995.
The lease obligation was already recorded on CP Rail's balance sheet and will not constitute additional financing, CBRS said.
The principal amount of series 1997-A1 is US$31.7 million, with principal payments starting January 13, 2007 and ending January 13, 2014.
The principal amount of series 1997-A2 is US$91.4 million, which will become due on January 13, 2014 with the initial and final payment occurring on that day.

CBRS said the A rating reflected the secure nature of the transaction, CP Rail's senior unsecured medium quality rating of B++ (high) and additional legal protection provided under the new Canadian transportation Act.

One section of the act enables the equipment trustee and its creditors to repossess the railway equipment from the operator in the event that it fails to meet obligations outlined in the trust indenture within 60 days, CBRS said.

It said the quality factors were partially offset by a high initial loan-to-value and the absence of any principal repayments for the first 10 years in the case of the series 1997-A1 holders, while the A2 holders do not receive repayment until the final distribution rate.
